subject: Geo-isolation & single-model mandate for Nimbus pilot (product decision needed)
messages:
From: Sara Khan <sara@nimbus.health>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot requirements - geo isolation + single model variant

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. To move to an internal sign-off we need two hard constraints for the pilot:

1) All inference must execute in the EU region (data residency + latency concerns). No cross-region fallback or routing to non-EU endpoints.
2) For consistency across regulators and our clinical validation, we need a forced single-model variant — the pilot must not automatically failover to other model families or quantized/optimized variants that change outputs.

These are non-negotiable for the initial 3-month pilot. Attached is a short security sheet that lists the requirement bullets. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate those restrictions and what trade-offs (latency/cost) you expect?

Sara Khan
Director, Integrations
Nimbus Health

Attachment: Nimbus_Security_Reqs.pdf

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sara Khan <sara@nimbus.health>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot requirements - geo isolation + single model variant

Hi Sara —

Appreciate the clarity. Short answer: we can support EU-only execution and a pinned single-model variant, but there are a few caveats I want to confirm with engineering/product before I commit to SLAs for the pilot:

- EU-only routing: we can pin requests to EU regions and prevent cross-region routing, but this reduces our ability to failover to other regions during a regional outage. We should document the availability trade-off.
- Single-model mandate: we can enforce a specific model id/version for the route. However, automatic optimizations (e.g., dynamic quantization or fallbacks to smaller variants under high load) would be disabled. That could increase cost and impact throughput under peak.

Looping in Jonas and Karthik to weigh in on operational risk and contract language.

Next step: Jonas — can you confirm operational constraints and recommend an approach (hard lock with manual fallback vs monitored canary that requires manual approval)?

Thanks,
Rachel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 08:36:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Pilot requirements - geo isolation + single model variant

Rachel / Karthik —

Thanks for the tag. Operational notes from runtime/product:

- EU-only routing: straightforward to implement at routing policy level (route-policy: region == eu AND customer == NIMBUS). We will mark the route as "no-fallback" so the router rejects capacity requests outside the EU. Impact: in case of EU-region capacity constraints or maintenance, the customer will see errors rather than a cross-region failover. Recommend an SLA carve-out in the pilot contract.

- Single-model mandate: we can pin a model id + exact variant (e.g., redwood/gptx-4.1:2026-01-17) and disable dynamic substitution. Downside: this prevents automatic remediations (e.g., swapping to a quantized variant during sustained load). For the pilot, I recommend a hybrid: enforce hard-pin for inference but enable a manual emergency fallback policy that requires two approved engineers to toggle. That preserves reproducibility for Nimbus while allowing admin-driven recovery.

- Throughput/cost: Expect token cost to be ~1.4x relative to our optimized multi-variant path and tail latency might increase under high concurrency due to lack of lighter fallbacks. We'll include batching and KV cache settings to mitigate.

I'll prepare a short ops note and change-request that lists exact router flags and the manual fallback playbook.

Jonas
Director, Product - Serving Runtime
